title: What AI tools are actually good for game development?
author: Nryquellts
selftext:
I’ve been using GPT Work for a lot of stuff and I tried Claude Code too, but I keep running into this point where they’re really useful for getting something started and then once the game gets bigger they start kinda losing the plot lol.

I’ve been thinking about trying Kimi Max next, so I wanted to see what everyone else is actually using and what has worked for you.

I’m not really trying to have AI just spit out an entire game for me. I mostly use it as scaffolding. Like I have the ideas and the kind of games I want to make, then I use AI to help me get prototypes running, work through systems, fix code, organize stuff, etc. Then I go through it and keep changing things until it actually feels like something I would want to play.

Long term I wanna make weirder systems-heavy games. Monster hunting, creature anatomy and part damage, ecology, investigation, tactical combat, strange fantasy/sci-fi stuff, PS2/PS3-ish visuals, things like that. Basically games where there’s actually a lot going on under the hood instead of just throwing a bunch of content at you.

Right now I’m also trying to make and release smaller games along the way. Partly just so I actually finish things and learn from shipping them, but also because if they make anything I can put that money straight back into subscriptions, assets, software and eventually the bigger games I actually wanna make.

I figure it’s better to start making stuff now with what I have instead of waiting years until I magically know everything.

So what are you guys using right now? GPT, Claude, Kimi, Codex, Gemini, whatever. I’m especially curious what holds up once your game gets past the tiny prototype stage and you actually have to maintain the thing.

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: I used Lattice to scaffold and from there has just been pure vibes. I think I’m enjoying the [reports](http://waypost.space) I’m having it produce more than the game at this point, though. They’re hilarious.

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: Kinda songs like you need to divide your project into parts instead of having one AI so the whole thing

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Maybe, yeah, I probably need to do that, I'll work up to that point, thanks.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: At an example from my project, I use one AI to help me design the game, created design vision.  I had another AI helped me create the skill system.  I had another AI helped me with NPC behavior.  I'm working with another AI to design the combat.  And I'm pretty aggressive about cutting context.

replies.author: Nryquellts
replies.body: Yeah that’s kinda the point, I’m using AI as scaffolding while I learn game design by actually making stuff but thanks anyway.

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
I use Claude Code for everything and a little bit of Codex. 

The game hasn't turned to slop yet and it's been months. You just gotta go slowly. Add one feature at a time, make sure to get other models to review the code, test the feature yourself. Iterate, cut stuff, expand stuff. Just go slowly and think through each new feature as much as possible.

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: I just use vscode and the codex and claude plugin. It can do anything.I did custom engine stuff too. I been doing unreal engine 5.8.
